options.option_text: Articulate (synonym — both mean expressing oneself fluently and clearly)
Inarticulate (correct: eloquent = fluent and persuasive; inarticulate = unable to express oneself clearly ✓)
Verbose (verbose = using more words than needed — extreme form, not opposite)
Loquacious (loquacious = talkative; related but not the direct antonym)

questions.explanation: B is correct. ELOQUENT = able to express ideas fluently and persuasively. Antonym = INARTICULATE = unable to speak clearly or express thoughts well. Synonyms of eloquent: articulate, expressive, persuasive, silver-tongued. Synonyms of inarticulate: incoherent, tongue-tied, mumbling.

options.option_text: Thrifty (synonym — both mean economical with money)
Economical (synonym — same meaning as frugal)
Extravagant (correct: frugal = careful and economical; extravagant = wasteful, spending excessively ✓)
Prudent (synonym in broader sense — includes being careful with money)

questions.explanation: C is correct. FRUGAL = careful and economical with money/resources. Antonym = EXTRAVAGANT = spending freely and excessively. Other antonyms: lavish, profligate, prodigal, wasteful. Common SSC exam trap: thrifty and economical look like antonyms because they're less extreme, but they're actually synonyms.

options.option_text: Sluggish (synonym — sluggish = slow-moving, similar to lethargic)
Listless (synonym — listless = lacking energy or enthusiasm)
Languid (synonym — languid = having disinclination for physical effort)
Energetic (correct: lethargic = sluggish, lacking energy; energetic = having or showing vigour ✓)

questions.explanation: D is correct. LETHARGIC = lacking energy or enthusiasm; sluggish. Antonym = ENERGETIC/VIGOROUS/DYNAMIC/VIVACIOUS. This is a synonym-trap question — all three wrong options are synonyms of lethargic. Synonyms of lethargic: sluggish, listless, languid, torpid, inert, apathetic.

options.option_text: Charitable (synonym — charitable = generous and kind, like benevolent)
Malevolent (correct: bene=good, male=bad, volent=wishing; malevolent = wishing harm ✓)
Philanthropic (synonym — both mean generous/charitable)
Magnanimous (synonym — magnanimous = generous/forgiving)

questions.explanation: B is correct. BENEVOLENT = well-meaning and kindly (bene=good + volent=wishing). Antonym = MALEVOLENT = having a wish to do evil (male=bad + volent=wishing). Memory: BENE = BENEFACTOR (good doer); MALE = MALEFACTOR (evil doer). Latin root pairs: bene/male appear often in vocabulary questions.

options.option_text: Transient (synonym — transient = lasting only briefly, like ephemeral)
Fleeting (synonym — fleeting = passing swiftly, short-lived)
Permanent (correct: ephemeral = lasting for only a short time; permanent = lasting indefinitely ✓)
Momentary (synonym — momentary = lasting only a moment)

questions.explanation: C is correct. EPHEMERAL = lasting for only a very short time (from Greek ephemeros = lasting a day). Antonym = PERMANENT/ETERNAL/PERPETUAL/ENDURING. All wrong options are synonyms of ephemeral — synonym-trap. 'Fame is ephemeral, character is permanent.'

options.option_text: Garrulous (synonym — garrulous = excessively talkative, like verbose)
Succinct (correct: verbose = using more words than needed; succinct = briefly and clearly expressed ✓)
Loquacious (synonym — loquacious = very talkative)
Prolix (synonym — prolix = using too many words)

questions.explanation: B is correct. VERBOSE = using more words than necessary. Antonym = SUCCINCT = briefly and clearly expressed. Other antonyms: terse, laconic, pithy, concise, brief. Key synonym-trap: garrulous, loquacious, and prolix are all synonyms of verbose.

options.option_text: Serene (synonym — serene = calm and peaceful)
Tranquil (synonym — tranquil = free from disturbance)
Turbulent (correct: placid = calm, unruffled; turbulent = disturbed, unsteady ✓)
Composed (synonym — composed = calm under pressure)

questions.explanation: C is correct. PLACID = not easily upset or excited; calm and peaceful. Antonym = TURBULENT = characterized by conflict, disorder, or confusion. Synonyms of placid: serene, tranquil, calm, unruffled, composed — all wrong options here. 'A placid lake' vs 'turbulent waters.'

options.option_text: Archaic (synonym — archaic = very old or outdated, like obsolete)
Contemporary (correct: obsolete = no longer in use; contemporary = belonging to the present time ✓)
Antiquated (synonym — antiquated = old-fashioned, out of date)
Outmoded (synonym — outmoded = out of fashion or out of date)

questions.explanation: B is correct. OBSOLETE = no longer produced or used; out of date. Antonym = CONTEMPORARY/CURRENT/MODERN. All wrong options are synonyms: archaic, antiquated, outmoded all mean old/out of date. 'Typewriters are obsolete; laptops are contemporary tools.'

options.option_text: Impoverished (synonym — both mean extremely poor)
Affluent (correct: destitute = extremely poor, without resources; affluent = wealthy ✓)
Indigent (synonym — indigent = poor, needy)
Penniless (synonym — penniless = having no money)

questions.explanation: B is correct. DESTITUTE = without the basic necessities of life; extremely poor. Antonym = AFFLUENT = having a great deal of money; wealthy. Other antonyms: prosperous, opulent, well-off, comfortable. The distractor options (impoverished, indigent, penniless) are all synonyms of destitute.

options.option_text: Native (synonym — indigenous and native both mean originating in a region)
Exotic (correct: indigenous = originating naturally in a place; exotic = from another country, unfamiliar ✓)
Endemic (synonym — endemic means native/specific to a region)
Aboriginal (synonym — another word for indigenous people)

questions.explanation: B is correct. INDIGENOUS = native to or originating naturally in a particular region. Antonym = EXOTIC = from another part of the world; not native. Other antonyms: foreign, alien, introduced, non-native. 'The tiger is indigenous to India; the zebra is exotic to India.'
